column1: # gerlach1252 key: Julius Kohn's key of 1889 (Wellcome MS.309 pp.260-261, scans 0265-0266) as set up by the contributor (key_v3), issue #439.

# The leaves carry rows of sign groups only, no letters; letter values come from the order of the groups (Z to A) and were re-aligned by the contributor where the text required (u, t, s groups are one step out of line, he says).

# key_v2 (16 Nov 2026, gerlach_keyfix/EVIDENCE.md): two signs of Kohn's sheet p.260 added that key_v3 omitted: OAR (k group, third sign: small o with a straight arrow) and 4C (l group, third sign: figure 4 with a curled foot, not yet seen in text). No existing value changed. Shape notes for ARW, SIG, MM, S3, 4L, 4U sharpened from the images; letter values unchanged.

column3: fe-like ligature (tall f + e); nearly always followed by C = "ch"
d-like: vertical stem with small triangle/loop on the left (reversed q)
small o with a tail rising steeply up to the right (sigma-like); often written touching a following SEVEN: SIG SEVEN = "de" (two signs; e.g. p.124 L01, p.130 L20, p.131 L02 "den")
> angle sign (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
ROUNDED cursive m (arched, like "m"), no stem or cross on top; e.g. p.16 L17. Not S3
g: small o joined by a level bar to a FLAT-topped 7-like hook (Kohn p.260 g group, first sign; e.g. p.130 L19 "finger"). Not SIG+SEVEN (d e), not OAR (k)
small o with a bar ending in a POINTED arrowhead or peaked hook (^), no flat top (Kohn p.260 k group, third sign; e.g. p.130 L20 "tecken", p.131 L04 "kesel")
OPEN figure 4: two separate strokes, top NOT closed (like a handwritten open "4" / "ч"); e.g. p.124 L02 "mol"
small o with cross-arm to the right (o+)
figure 4 with a curled foot (Kohn p.260 l group, third sign; Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
H-like, two posts with bar (often slanted)
reversed 3 / E with a middle bar, before u in "quecksilber" (p.115 heading) (probable)
CLOSED figure 4 with the stem through the middle, bottom ending in a point (kite / triangle on a cross)
ANGULAR pi/m-like sign with a vertical stroke rising through the top, often crossed (like Japanese "ホ"); Kohn p.260 s group, fourth sign; e.g. p.177 L04 and p.137 L20 "waser"

CLOSED figure 4 of modern/printed form: small closed triangle at upper left, bar running right, stem on the right with FLAT foot, no point (Kohn p.260 u group); the usual u/v sign from about p.40 on; e.g. p.124 L01 "und", p.137 L21 "buch"
circle with long vertical stroke (with or without a short crossbar)
4 with loop at top (like Greek koppa) (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
script capital L (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
Roman II / pi without overhang (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
upward arrow (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
reversed-J hook with crossbar (Kohn sheet only, not yet seen in text)
cross with bar on top (after TRI = tz)
